paragraphs: A solar garden torch is a stake with a lamp head on top, and the head has to do two jobs that fight each other: face the sky to charge and face down to light a path. The usual answer is a small panel on the crown with the light beneath it, which is why these lamps look top heavy.
The mesh is light at 22,158 polygons and 11,018 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the lamp head, the panel and the stake.
At $19 it suits garden and landscape visualisation, outdoor lighting retail renders, residential exterior scenes, evening and night imagery, and games. On sale since 2023.

A cable chain is the plainest link pattern there is: identical oval links, each at right angles to its neighbours. That simplicity is what makes it hard, because there is no ornament to distract from a link that is the wrong proportion or a join that does not close.
The mesh is efficient at 6,056 polygons and 6,137 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry entirely in the links.

A gold version sits on this page at the same $19. Both suit jewellery e-commerce and catalogue renders, luxury advertising, character set dressing for film, television and games, and product photography. Built to CheckMate specification, on sale since 2024.

Aquatic tape grass grows in long ribbons from a crown at the substrate, and the leaves twist as they rise and then lie along the surface once they run out of depth. That twist and that surface run are what make planted tank vegetation look alive rather than like blades stuck in gravel.
The mesh is light at 5,304 polygons and 5,414 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 2 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the translucent leaf and the vein structure.

At $19 and built to StemCell specification, it suits aquarium and aquascaping visualisation, underwater and freshwater scenes, pet retail renders, biology and education material, and games. On sale since 2018.

The thumbs up is probably the most used gesture symbol in the world, and its power comes from being unmistakable at any size. Translating it into three dimensions means giving the flat glyph a real hand shape without losing that instant readability - too much anatomy and it stops being a symbol.
The mesh is minimal at 625 polygons and 614 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 5 texture maps at 1024x1024. That tiny budget is exactly right for an icon.

A second build sits on this page at the same $19. Both suit motion graphics and interface work, social media and messaging content, advertising and explainer animation, and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2020.

A time capsule is a sealed cylinder with a screw or bolted lid and often a plaque with a date on it, designed to survive decades underground. The seal is the whole point, and it is why these are made from stainless steel or copper rather than from anything that will corrode.
The mesh is efficient at 30,752 polygons and 15,380 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the lid mechanism, the seal ring and the plaque.
At $19 it suits commemorative and ceremonial visualisation, school and institutional material, editorial and conceptual illustration, museum and heritage content, and games. On sale since 2023.

The foil hat is a visual joke that everyone recognises, and it works because of the material: crumpled aluminium catching light in a hundred directions, folded into a cone with an uneven brim. The irregularity is the whole effect - a smooth metallic cone reads as a party hat.
The mesh is minimal at 2,702 polygons and 2,791 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 7 texture maps at 1024x1024 carrying the creased foil surface.

At $19 and built to StemCell specification, it suits editorial and satirical illustration, motion graphics and social content, advertising with a comic register, character props for games and film, and print. On sale since 2020.

A clear bottle with liquid in it is two refractive materials meeting: the plastic wall and the water inside, with an air gap at the top and a meniscus where they meet. Modelling the water as its own body rather than filling the bottle shell is the only way any of that behaves correctly.
The mesh is minimal at 2,862 polygons and 2,759 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, sensible on a symmetrical moulded bottle, and the water is a separate body.

At $19 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits beverage packaging visualisation, brand and label mockups, retail and e-commerce renders, table and desk set dressing, and games. On sale since 2026.

A neck pillow is a horseshoe that has to close enough to support the chin without choking, which is why the gap at the front is so specific. Filled with beads or foam it sags at the back and stands up at the ends, and that asymmetry is what makes it read as a used object.
The mesh is minimal at 2,136 polygons and 1,078 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a soft form whose realism comes from the fabric material.
At $19 it suits travel and aviation visualisation, luggage and accessory retail renders, airport and cabin scenes, lifestyle imagery and games. On sale since 2023.

A banded bundle of notes is a very specific object: the notes compress at the band and fan slightly at the free edge, and the stack is never perfectly square. That slight disorder is what separates cash from a printed block, and it is where all of the modelling goes.
The mesh is minimal at 430 polygons and 432 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is exactly the right economy for a subject that reads entirely through its printed surface.

At $19 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits financial and banking visualisation, editorial and news illustration, advertising and print, thriller and crime set dressing, and games. On sale since 2024.

Structural bonding tape is thicker than ordinary double sided tape because the foam core is doing the work: it spreads load and absorbs movement between two panels. That thickness is visible at the roll edge, and it is what distinguishes the product from a thin adhesive film.
The mesh is minimal at 1,308 polygons and 1,304 vertices, built entirely from quads with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the roll form and the liner edge.
At $19 it suits industrial and manufacturing product visualisation, hardware and trade retail renders, workshop and production scenes, packaging mockups and games. On sale since 2022.

Ice cleats are an elastic harness carrying steel spikes or coils, stretched over a boot rather than built into it. Shown mounted, the harness is under tension and follows the sole contour, which is quite different from the flat ring the product is in its packaging.

The mesh is light at 9,350 polygons and 9,494 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, sensible on a subject built from repeated spikes and a symmetrical harness, and the StemCell build means it works in a real-time engine.
At $19 it suits winter and outdoor equipment visualisation, footwear retail renders, safety and workplace material, hiking and mountaineering imagery, and games. On sale since 2026.

A shipping crate is built from slats with gaps between them, because a solid box would cost more timber and weigh more without adding strength. The frame takes the load, the slats hold the contents, and the corner blocks are what let crates be stacked without crushing.
The mesh is efficient at 16,648 polygons and 16,778 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the slats, the frame joints and the fixings.
At $19 it suits logistics and warehouse visualisation, port and freight scenes, industrial and market set dressing, film and television, and games. On sale since 2024.

A cling wrapped supermarket tray is a specific and instantly readable object: a shallow foam tray with film pulled tight over the top, gathered and tucked underneath, with a printed label on one corner. The film creases in a starburst where it was stretched, and that pattern is the whole giveaway.
The model is built from ngons at 2,169 polygons and 2,185 vertices with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 4 texture maps at 2048x2048 carrying the film sheen and the foam texture.

At $19 and built to StemCell specification, it suits supermarket and food retail visualisation, packaging and label mockups, food photography set dressing, kitchen scenes and games. On sale since 2019.

A drum cradle grips a barrel around its rim and lets one person tip it to pour, which is safer than wrestling a full drum by hand. The lever handle multiplies the effort, the cradle holds the drum at the balance point, and the frame keeps it from rolling once tipped.
The mesh runs 59,172 polygons and 60,188 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the cradle arms, the lever mechanism and the frame.
At $18 it suits industrial handling and warehouse visualisation, chemical and fuel handling scenes, safety and training material, equipment marketing and games. On sale since 2021.
